veranderings.rede: The separable compound verb 'binneroep' is written as one word.

veranderings.voor: Palesa is toe al in die kombuis
veranderings.na: Palesa is reeds in die kombuis
veranderings.rede: The story is told in the present tense, so the past-tense marker 'toe' clashes; 'reeds' keeps the meaning.

veranderings.voor: begin Ouma se regterpols seer trek by die eerste paar druk
veranderings.na: begin Ouma se regterpols seer word sodra sy die eerste paar keer druk
veranderings.rede: 'seer trek by die eerste paar druk' is unidiomatic, and 'druk' as a count noun would need the plural 'drukke'.
The Afrikaans idiom for a quarter turn is ''n kwartslag draai'.
Keeps the tense consistent with the present-tense narrative and the 'word' in the same sentence.
'n tweede paar hande' calques English 'a second pair of hands'; 'nog 'n paar hande' is the natural Afrikaans.
A hinge that has come out of a post has 'losgeruk'; plain 'geruk' reads as if something pulled it.

veranderings.voor: heen en weer en dit hang
veranderings.na: heen en weer, en dit hang
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: a comma before 'en' joining two clauses that each have their own subject and verb.
Afrikaans uses 'om' with a time of day: 'om dieselfde tyd'.

veranderings.na: vra hoe dit met haar pols gaan
veranderings.rede: 'vra na haar pols' is stiff; asking how her wrist is doing is the natural, grade-appropriate phrasing.

veranderings.voor: na Pa toe by die hek
veranderings.na: na Pa by die hek toe
veranderings.rede: The circumposition 'na ... toe' should enclose the whole place phrase.

veranderings.voor: Ouma skink vir haar 'n koppie koffie
veranderings.na: Ouma skink vir haarself 'n koppie koffie
veranderings.rede: Palesa is named in the sentence before, so 'vir haar' could mean Palesa; 'haarself' makes clear Ouma pours it for herself.
No chair is mentioned anywhere, so 'daardie stoel' has nothing to refer to; 'daar' points back to the doorway.

vlae.teks: Ouma skink vir haar 'n koppie koffie en gaan sit in die deur. Van daardie stoel af kan sy die kombuis en die hek sien.
vlae.rede: The last sentence refers to 'daardie stoel', but the lesson never mentions a chair. A sentence about one may have been cut. I proposed 'Van daar af' as a language-only fix. If the chair is meant to be in the story, the writer should restore it.
